title: 63 Years Ago This Week, Félicette Became the First Cat in Space - Nautilus
gist: On October 18, 1963, French cat Felicette became the first cat in space, flying above 150 km for about five minutes of weightlessness and landing safely by parachute. She was picked from 14 trained cats.

insights.claim: Felicette flew above 150 km (93 miles) on October 18, 1963, with about five minutes of weightlessness, on a trip under 20 minutes, and landed safely by parachute.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Historical space-biology trivia with little market relevance.

insights.claim: The flight did not reach orbit, but it went higher than Blue Origin's New Shepard with Jeff Bezos aboard and about 40 percent of the way to the International Space Station.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.locator: It wasn't enough to get into orbit

insights.claim: Felicette was chosen from 14 cats, apparently for her relaxed temperament, after months of training in harnesses up to two hours a day with simulated flight sounds.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Shows temperament-based selection was used in early animal spaceflight.
